uncited: Neural and Implicit Representations render scenes by evaluating continuous scalar fields—parameterized as neural networks, Gaussian mixtures, or radial basis functions—along camera rays to compute geometry and appearance [Ray-marching on 3D Gaussians](1036-ray-marching-on-3d-gaussians.md), [Ray Marching with Neural SDF](2409-ray-marching-with-neural-sdf.md), [RBF Particle Volume Path Tracing](9641-rbf-particle-volume-path-tracing.md), and [MetaNLR++](15259-metanlr.md).

Unlike [Raymarching with Depth Buffer Occlusion](1880-raymarching-with-depth-buffer-occlusion.md) and [Acceleration and Optimization](6222-acceleration-and-optimization.md), which rely on explicit depth buffers, voxel grids, or BVH acceleration, this family evaluates continuous implicit functions directly along rays, trading computational overhead for geometric continuity and data-driven reconstruction.
* Step: Pre-compute near-far bounds for each ray by counting the minimum and maximum distances of ray-to-mesh intersections.
* Layout: Model Architecture: Geometry Code $l_g(x)$ (dim 32), Texture Code $l_t(x)$ (dim 32), Sign Distance $h(x)$ (dim 1).
Interpolated Items include $l_t(x)$ (dim 32), gradient of SDF $|\nabla_x s|$ (dim 256), $s$ (dim 256), $\gamma$ (dim 256), $h(x)$ (dim 1), $d$ (dim 160), $\gamma$ (dim 32).
MetaNLR++ leverages meta-learning with the Reptile algorithm to accelerate convergence on new scenes [MetaNLR++](15259-metanlr.md).
